relationships.description: The motion definition animates the UI into the target experience state, so the state's entry is presented through this template's animation type, duration and easing.
relationships.evidence: A state machine definition (e.g. an XState state node or a state config) references the transition template by name as its enter animation, or the CSS/Framer Motion variant keyed to that state imports the shared template.

relationships.description: The motion definition carries the UI into the sub-view region, animating that region's enter or leave within its parent view.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view's markup or component wrapper (e.g. an AnimatePresence or Vue <Transition> around the region) is configured with the shared template's name, duration and easing tokens.

relationships.description: The motion definition dictates how the state transition is visually animated when it fires, without determining which event or guard causes the transition.
relationships.evidence: The state transition's specification or code declares an animation/transition property pointing to the template id, and the rendered animation uses the template's duration and easing values.

relationships.description: The motion definition is used to animate the route change that brings the user to the view, governing how the view appears when navigated to.
relationships.evidence: The router configuration or route entry for the view (e.g. a route meta transition field or page transition wrapper) names the template as the animation applied on navigation to that view.

relationships.description: The more specific motion definition is a variant of a base template, inheriting its animation type, duration and easing and overriding only some of them.
relationships.evidence: The design-token or motion spec declares the template with an extends/base reference to another template, or the animation config object spreads the base template and overrides selected properties.

relationships.description: Completion or a lifecycle point of the animation defined by the template initiates the state action, such as navigating or closing once the exit animation finishes.
relationships.evidence: An animation-end callback (e.g. onAnimationComplete, transitionend listener, or onAfterLeave hook) tied to the template dispatches or invokes the state action.

notes: A TransitionTemplate describes how a change animates, not which change occurs, so flows-to ExperienceState/SubView and navigates-to View misstate its role; applies (template applied to these elements) fits better and would be consistent across targets. triggers StateAction conflicts with StateAction being executed by state/transition lifecycle hooks, not animations. governs StateTransition also overlaps with applies.
